does: Sends an entity's animation blueprint the gameplay event ASAnimation (id d6c855f3-a9c0-45dc-86dd-d3da429e33b1): arguments 0 to 2 are the start, loop and end sets of animation short names, 3 a float, 4 a flag. The third parameter is the event as a tuple laid out last member first: flag at +0, float at +4, end set at +8, loop set at +0x20, start set at +0x38; the arrays are moved out of the sets.

evidence.says: It builds an event description with the id global the init of the gameplay events fills from the string d6c855f3-..., writes the flag and the float as arguments 4 and 3, and +0x1BC5130 moves the three sets into arguments 2, 1 and 0 before the generic TriggerGameplayEvent; the macOS build names the same code TriggerGameplayEvent<EoCGE::ASAnimation>.

A probe while Osi.PlayAnimation runs on the host shows 2 calls, one of them from the client's sender at +0x1BC4C50. Called for a client-only timeline dummy with one linked animation in the start set, the figure plays it: text keys, root motion and an end.
the macOS build's symbols hold this name; it is tied to this function by the job its read shows
